title: CAD Weakens on Widening US-Canada Rate Gap
body: The Canadian dollar edged down to around 1.41 per US dollar in September, its weakest level in more than a month, as investors anticipated a widening interest-rate gap between the US and Canada. Markets expect the Federal Reserve to continue tightening policy while the Bank of Canada leaves rates on hold. At its most recent meeting, the Fed raised its federal funds target range, further enhancing the US dollar's yield advantage over the loonie. In contrast, the BoC kept its key policy rate unchanged at 2.25% in September. Persistently high oil prices are adding upward pressure on Canadian inflation, though this may be tempered by economic slack linked to trade tensions with the US. Canadian retail sales are estimated to have risen 1.3% month over month in August, recovering from a decline in July. If confirmed, this would be the strongest increase since January and may point to resilient domestic demand. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Brazilian Real Strengthens Following Inflation Data
body: The Brazilian real edged up to 5.12 per US dollar in September after stronger-than-expected mid-month inflation data. Mid-month headline inflation accelerated to 4.47% year over year, up from 4.24% previously and above the 4.30% market consensus. Persistent inflationary pressures may limit room for further cuts in the Selic rate, as the 12-month inflation rate has moved back above the upper bound of the BCB's target range. At its September meeting, the BCB lowered the policy rate by 25 bps to 13.75% and left future decisions open, while the Copom minutes struck a more hawkish tone than anticipated. Externally, oil prices declined, easing some energy-related inflation pressures. Even so, the global backdrop remained challenging, with international yields climbing above recent historical ranges before pausing their rise in response to the oil correction. The US Federal Reserve raised its federal funds target rate at its latest meeting, and the narrowing interest-rate differential continues to provide support for the US dollar. title: Brazil 10-Year Yield Falls as Global Surge Eases
body: Brazil's 10-year government bond yield eased to 14.1% in late September, as a drop in oil prices helped halt the sharp sell-off in global bonds. Lower oil prices tempered inflation concerns and temporarily paused the broader bond-market correction, amid expectations of progress in diplomatic talks between Iran and the United States. At the same time, domestic developments exerted upward pressure on yields. Brazil's mid-month headline inflation accelerated to 4.47% year over year in September, up from 4.24% previously and above the 4.30% market consensus. Persistent inflationary pressures could diminish the likelihood of a continued Selic easing cycle. The Banco Central do Brasil cut its policy rate by 25 bps to 13.75% at its September meeting and left its forward guidance deliberately open, while the Copom minutes struck a more hawkish tone than markets had anticipated. title: TSX Rises as Global Yield Surge Pauses
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index rose 0.3% to close at 35,801 on Friday, trimming earlier losses as easing oil prices helped halt the recent surge in global bond yields. Crude and fuel prices retreated after reports that the US and Iran had made progress toward an agreement to lift naval blockades on tankers in the Persian Gulf and to relax certain economic sanctions on Tehran. Benchmark borrowing costs also pulled back after touching multi-year highs on Thursday. Financials advanced, with major banks finishing higher: RBC and TD Bank each gained 1.2%, BMO added 0.8%, Scotiabank rose 1.5%, and CIBC climbed 2%. Mining stocks were mixed. Gold prices rose on the day but still logged a weekly decline. Barrick advanced 1.5%, while Kinross rebounded 2.8% after slumping more than 10% on Thursday, when the company cut its production outlook for 2026 and 2027. In contrast, WPM and Franco-Nevada each slipped 0.7%. Energy heavyweights weakened in response to lower oil prices. Overall, the index finished the week little changed. title: US Stocks Rise as Oil Pullback Halts Yield Surge
body: US stock indices finished higher on Friday as a pullback in oil prices helped halt the recent surge in Treasury yields. Benchmark borrowing costs paused their climb after hitting multi-decade highs on Thursday. Performance among AI-related stocks was mixed. Hardware names were mostly higher: Applied Materials rose 2.3%, and Lam Research gained 2.6%. Meta fell 3.3% on the day but still finished the week with a gain following a series of hardware announcements tied to its Muse AI agent. Oracle declined 1.7%. Financial stocks were mostly stronger.
